subject: Discovery — next meeting & trial kickoff windows (prompt pack preview)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@aureliahealth.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery — next meeting & trial kickoff windows (prompt pack preview)

Hi Tom / Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can lock in the evaluation kickoff:

Recap (brief):
- Primary use case: automated claims summarization + compliance tagging for pre-approval workflows.
- Key constraints: <24h retention for PII-free payloads, SSO with SAML, on-prem connector for records sync.
- Success signals you mentioned: 95% precision on tag mappings, <1s latency on single-record inference at 512 tokens, and clear ROI baseline (reduced manual triage time).

Proposed next step: 60–90 minute evaluation kickoff / technical deep dive where we:
1) Walk through the trial plan & roles (internal owners, data access, timeline)
2) Share the prompt pack and initial evals to validate quality
3) Discuss connectors, auth (SSO/KMS), and security posture
4) Align on success criteria and go/no-go decision gates

Available windows (PT):
- Thu Jul 22 — 10:00–11:00
- Thu Jul 22 — 16:00–17:00
- Fri Jul 23 — 09:00–10:00

Attachments: redwood-eval-charter.pdf (charter + proposed timeline), prompt-pack-sample.csv (3 sample prompts & scoring rubric).

If any of those slots work, pick one and I’ll send the invite. If not, feel free to propose two alternatives and we’ll accommodate. I’ve cc’d Karthik (solutions) to lead the technical deep dive.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the trial started.

—
Aditya Rao

Redwood Inference

Thanks, Aditya — good call today. Quick answers and a couple of asks before we lock time: 

Availability: Thu Jul 22 10:00–11:00 PT works best for our team (Tom, Sarah + engineering lead Maya).

Pre-kickoff asks:
- Can you share a short list of the success criteria you normally surface for a claims use case? We want the rubric early so our PMs can prepare acceptance tests.
- Security: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short checklist of what data remains in our environment vs. Redwood’s hosted layers during the eval.
- Data access: the initial plan is to run on a small anonymized subset (S3 export). We may want to discuss an on-prem connector later.

I attached a one-pager with our compliance contacts (SOC2-request.xlsx) and pasted a couple of items from the discovery notes below.

Perfect — Thu Jul 22 10:00–11:00 PT is on our side as well. I’ll send a calendar invite to the attendees you listed (Tom, Sarah, Maya).

Quick notes before the kickoff so everyone is aligned:
- Roles: Karthik will run the technical deep dive (connectors, SSO/KMS, quantization options). Marissa Cole (cc’d) from CS will cover trial ops and success criteria / evaluation scoring.
- Success criteria (working draft):
  * Precision on compliance tags >= 95% across the sample set
  * Mean inference latency < 1s @ 512 tokens in your target environment
  * Prompt-stability: <5% variance in top-label agreement across 1000 prompts
  * Clear operator workflow to reduce manual triage time by at least 30%

Prep items for Aurelia Health:
- Provide the anonymized S3 export and a sample mapping document for the tags (S3 link or SFTP).
- Confirm SSO type (SAML/OIDC) and whether we should include your security contact on the kickoff.
- Any existing test prompts you want us to include in the prompt-pack preview.

I’ve attached the charter and a small prompt pack sample to this thread. Calendar invite will include a short agenda.

If you want, I can also add a short tech-ops appendix to the charter that outlines the data flow during the trial (what stays in your environment vs. what Redwood processes).

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
